entities.summary: Richard Burdon Haldane, 1st Viscount Haldane, was a Scottish lawyer, philosopher, influential Liberal and later Labour politician and statesman. He was Secretary of State for War between 1905 and 1912 during which time the "Haldane Reforms" of the British Army were implemented. As Secretary of State of War, he was instrumental in founding MI5, MI6, the Territorial Army, the British Expeditionary Force, and the Royal Flying Corps. Beyond his military contributions, Haldane was a significant figure in education, contributing to the founding of institutions such as Imperial College London and the London School of Economics.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As Secretary of State for War, Haldane implemented the 'Haldane Reforms' that modernized the British Army and laid the groundwork for future military reforms. His contributions to education also had lasting impacts on institutions such as Imperial College London.
